items.title: 6.11 Real Life Problems involving Sequences and Series

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
This section uses what you already know (A.P. and G.P. terms and sums) in everyday situations: loans, savings, screen design and lease payments. The mathematics is not new; the skill is to translate words into a sequence.
Ask two questions every time: (1) Does the quantity change by adding the same amount (A.P.) or by multiplying by the same factor (G.P.)? (2) Does the question want one particular term or the total (sum)?

rows: Amount grows by the same number each step (simple interest, fixed increase)
Amount grows by the same percentage each step (compound interest, growth)

Simple Interest on Loan (Arithmetic Sequence with Particular Term)

blocks.title: Example 29
blocks.problem: To buy furniture for a new apartment Tayyab borrowed Rs. 50,000 at 8% simple interest for 11 years. How much interest will he pay?
steps:
Given: principal Rs. 50,000, simple interest rate 8% per year, time 11 years.
To find: the total interest after 11 years.
Method: with simple interest the same amount is added every year, so the total interest after 1, 2, 3, ... years forms an A.P.; we need its \(11^{\text{th}}\) term.

Step 1: Interest after one and two years
\[50000 \times \dfrac{8}{100} \times 1 = 4000\]
\[50000 \times \dfrac{8}{100} \times 2 = 8000\]
Why: simple interest \(= \) principal \(\times\) rate \(\times\) time; it is always worked out on the original Rs. 50,000.

Step 2: Recognise the A.P.
\[4000, 8000, 12000, \dots\]
\[a_{1} = 4000,\ d = 8000 - 4000 = 4000\]
\[n = 11\]
Why: each year adds the same Rs. 4000, so the totals increase by a common difference.

Check:
\[50000 \times \dfrac{8}{100} \times 11 = 44000\]
The simple interest formula gives the same answer.
blocks.answer: Tayyab will pay a total interest of Rs. 44000 on the borrowed amount of Rs. 50,000 after 11 years.

blocks.text: Compound Interest on Loan (Geometric Sequence with Particular Term)

blocks.title: Example 30
blocks.problem: Amna invests Rs. 200000 at 5% interest compounded annually. What total amount will she get after 10 years?
steps:
Given: principal \(P = \) Rs. 200000, rate 5% per year compounded annually, 10 years.
To find: the total amount after 10 years.
Method: with compound interest each year's amount is multiplied by the same factor \(1.05\), so the yearly amounts form a G.P.; we need its \(10^{\text{th}}\) term.

Step 1: The first year
\[\text{Interest} = P \times \dfrac{5}{100} = P(0.05)\]
\[\text{Amount} = P + P(0.05) = P(1 + 0.05)\]
Why: the amount at the end of a year is the principal plus that year's interest.

Step 2: The second year
\[\text{Interest} = P(1 + 0.05) \times 0.05\]
\[\text{Amount} = P(1.05) + P(1.05)(0.05)\]
\[= P(1 + 0.05)(1 + 0.05)\]
\[= P(1 + 0.05)^{2}\]
Why: "compounded" means interest is now earned on the whole amount of the first year, not on \(P\) only. Taking \(P(1.05)\) common gives \((1 + 0.05)\) again.

Step 3: Recognise the G.P.
Similarly the amount after the third year is \(P(1 + 0.05)^{3}\), so the amounts are
\[P(1.05), P(1.05)^{2}, P(1.05)^{3}, \dots\]
a G.P. with \(a_{1} = P(1.05)\), \(r = 1.05\), \(n = 10\). (The book prints the first term as \(a_{l} = P(1.05)\), see the correction below.)
Why: each amount is the previous one times \(1.05\).

Step 5: Calculate
\[(1.05)^{10} = 1.62889\ (\text{approx.})\]
\[(200000)(1.62889)\]
The book writes \(= 325778.92\).
Why: a calculator gives \((1.05)^{10} = 1.6288946...\). With all the decimals, \(200000 \times 1.6288946... = 325778.925...\), which rounds to \(325778.93\); see the correction below.

Check:
Amount after 1 year \(= 210000\), after 2 years \(= 220500\) (\(= 210000 \times 1.05\)). The amounts keep growing by 5% of the previous amount, as a G.P. should.
blocks.answer: Amna will get about Rs. 325778.93 after 10 years (the book prints Rs. 325778.92).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text:
1. In Example 30 the book prints the first term as \(a_{l} = P(1.05)\) (a letter l); it should be \(a_{1} = P(1.05)\), the first term.
2. The book gives the final amount as Rs. 325778.92. Rounded correctly to two decimal places, \(200000(1.05)^{10} = 325778.925...\) is Rs. 325778.93 (and using the rounded \(1.62889\) gives Rs. 325778.00). The difference is one paisa.
Grid Column Distribution (Arithmetic Series Sum of Terms)

blocks.title: Example 31
blocks.problem: A web designer is using a 12-column grid system where each column increases in width by \(10px\) from the previous one. The first column width is \(50px\) wide. Find the total width occupied by all 12 columns.
steps:
Given: 12 columns; first width \(50px\); each column \(10px\) wider than the previous one.
To find: the total width of all 12 columns.
Method: the widths \(50, 60, 70, \dots\) form an A.P., and "total width" is a sum, so we use the A.P. sum formula.

Step 1: Identify the A.P.
\[a_{1} = 50,\quad d = 10,\quad n = 12\]
Why: "increases by \(10px\)" means the same amount is added each time: a common difference.

Step 2: Use the sum formula
\[S_{n} = \dfrac{n}{2}[2a_{1} + (n-1)d]\]
\[S_{12} = \dfrac{12}{2}[2(50) + (12-1)(10)]\]
Why: we need the total of all 12 terms, not just the last term.
blocks.answer: The total width of all 12 columns is \(1260px\).

blocks.title: Example 32
blocks.problem:
Motor Vehicle Leasing Using Arithmetic Sequence
A company leases a motor vehicle with the following terms:
• The first monthly payment is Rs. 15,000
• Each subsequent payment increases by Rs. 500 due to inflation adjustments.
• The lease term is 24 months.
Find:
(i) What is the payment in the \(24^{\text{th}}\) month?
(ii) What is the total amount paid over 24 months?
(iii) If the company can only afford to pay a total of Rs. 400,000, can they complete the 24-months lease?
(iv) Find maximum months \(n\) such that total, payment \(S_{n} \le 400,000\).
steps:
Given: first term \(a_{1} = 15000\), common difference \(d = 500\), number of terms \(n = 24\).
To find: (i) \(a_{24}\); (ii) \(S_{24}\); (iii) whether \(S_{24} \le 400000\); (iv) the largest \(n\) with \(S_{n} \le 400000\).
Method: monthly payments rising by a fixed Rs. 500 form an A.P.; (i) is a term, (ii) a sum, (iii) a comparison, (iv) a quadratic inequality.

Step 1 (i): Payment in the \(24^{\text{th}}\) month
\[a_{n} = a_{1} + (n-1)d\]
\[a_{24} = 15000 + (24-1)(500)\]
\[= 15000 + 23 \times 500\]
\[= 15000 + 11500 = 26500\]
Why: the payment in a particular month is one term of the A.P.

Step 2 (ii): Total over 24 months
\[S_{n} = \dfrac{n}{2}(a_{1} + a_{n})\]
\[S_{24} = \dfrac{24}{2}(15000 + 26500)\]
\[= 12(41500) = 498000\]
Why: \(S_{n} = \frac{n}{2}(a_{1} + a_{n})\) (first term plus last term) is quickest because we already know \(a_{24}\). The book prints the formula as \(S_{n} = \frac{n}{2}(a_{n} + a_{n})\), see the correction below.

Step 3 (iii): Can they afford it?
\[498000 > 400000\]
\[498000 - 400000 = 98000\]
Why: the total needed is more than the budget, so the answer is No; the shortfall is Rs. 98,000.

Step 4 (iv): Set up the inequality
\[S_{n} = \dfrac{n}{2}[2a_{1} + (n-1)d] \le 400000\]
\[\dfrac{n}{2}[2(15000) + (n-1)(500)] \le 400000\]
Why: here \(n\) is unknown, so we use the sum formula that needs only \(a_{1}\) and \(d\).

Step 5 (iv): Simplify to a quadratic
\[n[15000 + 250n - 250] \le 400000\]
\[n(250n + 14750) \le 400000\]
\[250n^{2} + 14750n - 400000 \le 0\]
\[n^{2} + 59n - 1600 \le 0\]
Why: dividing the bracket by 2 removes \(\frac{1}{2}\); then expand, bring everything to one side and divide by \(250\) (positive, so \(\le\) stays).

Step 6 (iv): Solve the associated equation
\[n^{2} + 59n - 1600 = 0\]
\[n = \dfrac{-59 \pm \sqrt{(59)^{2} - 4(1)(-1600)}}{2(1)}\]
\[n = \dfrac{-59 \pm 99.4}{2}\]
\[n = -79.2,\quad n = 20.2\]
Why: the quadratic formula gives where \(n^{2} + 59n - 1600\) is zero; \(\sqrt{3481 + 6400} = \sqrt{9881} \approx 99.4\).

Step 7 (iv): Choose \(n\)
The expression is \(\le 0\) between the roots, i.e. for \(-79.2 \le n \le 20.2\). A number of months is a positive whole number, so the largest is
\[n = 20\]
Why: \(n = 20\) satisfies the inequality and \(n = 21\) does not.
blocks.answer: (i) Rs. 26500; (ii) Rs. 498000; (iii) No, the total exceeds the budget by Rs. 98,000; (iv) \(n = 20\) months.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: In Example 32 (ii) the book prints the formula as \(S_{n} = \frac{n}{2}(a_{n} + a_{n})\). It should be \(S_{n} = \frac{n}{2}(a_{1} + a_{n})\) (first term plus last term). The book's numbers \(\frac{24}{2}(15000 + 26500)\) already use the correct formula.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. Fixed increase each step (simple interest, Rs. 500 more each month, 10px wider): A.P.
2. Fixed percentage growth (compound interest): G.P. with \(r = 1 + \frac{\text{rate}}{100}\).
3. "In the \(n^{\text{th}}\) month / after \(n\) years" asks for a term; "total" asks for a sum.
4. When \(n\) is the unknown in a sum, you get a quadratic; keep only the positive whole-number answer that fits.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text:
1. Using the A.P. formula for compound interest: compound interest multiplies, so it is a G.P.
2. Giving the last term when the total is asked (Example 31 asks for all 12 columns, not the \(12^{\text{th}}\)).
3. Rounding \(n = 20.2\) up to \(21\): \(S_{21}\) already exceeds the budget. Round down and check.
4. Writing \(5\%\) as \(5\) or \(1.5\): the growth factor is \(1 + 0.05 = 1.05\).
